- When sentiment is positive (≥ 0.5) in the last 3–5 days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 2–5% for next 7–14 days.  
- When sentiment is negative (≤ -0.5) in the last 3–5 days, model tends to underestimate prices; increase forecast by 2–5% for next 7–14 days.  
- Model consistently overreacts to recent price spikes (e.g., +10%+ in 3–5 days) by overshooting 5–10% in the next 5–7 days; apply a 5–10% downward correction.  
- Model underestimates mean-reversion periods (e.g., after 3–5 consecutive days of price decline) by 3–8%; adjust upward by 3–8% for next 5–10 days.  
- For 30-day forecasts, model often fails to capture sentiment-driven momentum; if sentiment is trending, align forecast slope with sentiment direction (e.g., if sentiment rises, forecast should rise at least 1–2% per day).  
- If last 3–5 days show no sentiment change, model tends to drift toward historical mean; apply mean-reversion correction by 1–3% per day for next 5–7 days.
